review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

25:1.sourceText: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
25:1.targetText: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause (λαβοῦσαι, "having taken") to the main verb went out.

25:2.sourceText: πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι.
25:2.targetText: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

groups.note: The one ἦσαν is understood again in the second clause, where BSB repeats were.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

25:3.sourceText: αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
25:3.targetText: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.

groups.note: μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, "with themselves", is rendered along.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the explanatory γάρ ("for") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a text with αὐτῶν ("their") after λαμπάδας; N1904 has no possessive here.
English joins the participle clause (λαβοῦσαι, "having taken") to the main verb with a contrast.
English clarifies the contrast; the Greek has only ἔλαιον ("oil").

25:4.sourceText: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

groups.note: The genitive absolute participle χρονίζοντος is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

25:6.sourceText: μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν.
25:6.targetText: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

groups.note: μέσης νυκτός, "in the middle of the night", is rendered At midnight.
γέγονεν, "there came" (a cry), is rendered rang out.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of meet; N1904 has no αὐτοῦ here (the Byzantine text adds it).

25:7.sourceText: τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν.
25:7.targetText: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the demonstrative ἐκεῖναι ("those") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

25:8.sourceText: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB marks the causal ὅτι ("because") with a semicolon only.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

25:9.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι Μή ποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
25:9.targetText: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθησαν … λέγουσαι, "answered, saying", is rendered said.
Μή ποτε ("lest") introduces the feared outcome, rendered or … may.
The emphatic double negative οὐ μή is rendered not.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the refusal implied by the answer; the Greek begins with Μή ποτε ("lest").
English adds both for emphasis; the Greek has only ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν.
English supplies the object of sell; the Greek participle has none.
English supplies the object of buy; the Greek verb has none.

25:10.targetText: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.

groups.note: The genitive absolute participle ἀπερχομένων is rendered as a while-clause.
The article with the adjective, "the ready ones", is rendered as a relative clause.

25:11.sourceText: ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν.
25:11.targetText: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’

BSB leaves καί ("also": the rest also came) untranslated.

25:12.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
25:12.targetText: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

groups.note: The article ὁ is used as a pronoun.
ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν, "answering said", is rendered replied.

25:13.sourceText: Γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν.
25:13.targetText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.

groups.note: After the negative, οὐδέ ("nor") is rendered or.

25:14.sourceText: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ,
25:14.targetText: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.

groups.note: ἰδίους, "his own", is rendered his.
παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, "handed over to them the possessions", is rendered entrusted them with his possessions.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek comparison Ὥσπερ ("just as") has no main clause of its own.
English turns the main verb ἐκάλεσεν into a relative clause.

25:15.sourceText: καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα, ᾧ δὲ δύο, ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν. Εὐθέως
25:15.targetText: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent—each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.

groups.note: The one τάλαντα is understood again with two and one, where BSB repeats the noun.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The correlative μέν has no English counterpart.
BSB leaves this δέ untranslated and lists the second servant with a comma.

groups.note: The article with the participle λαβών, "the one who received", is rendered The servant who had received.
N1904 prints Εὐθέως at the end of 25:15.
ἐν αὐτοῖς, "with them", is rendered as the object of put to work.

25:17.sourceText: ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the link the elliptical Greek ("the one … the two") leaves understood.

25:42.sourceText: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με,
25:42.targetText: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink,

groups.note: The negative οὐκ ("did not give me to eat") is rendered gave me nothing.
The negative οὐκ is rendered gave me nothing.
ποτίζω, "give to drink", is rendered gave … to drink.

25:43.sourceText: ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
25:43.targetText: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb the Greek leaves understood with γυμνός ("naked").
English supplies the verb the Greek leaves understood with ἀσθενής ("sick").

25:44.sourceText: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
25:44.targetText: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’

groups.note: τότε ("then") is rendered loosely as And.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the quotation.

25:45.sourceText: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ’ ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
25:45.targetText: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’

groups.note: ἐφ’ ὅσον, "inasmuch as", is rendered whatever.
οὐδέ, "neither / not even", is rendered not.

unmappedSource.reason: The addressee αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not expressed in English.
The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the quotation.

25:46.sourceText: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
25:46.targetText: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
